content:
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially near end of horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent spikes (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then corrects; cap forecasts at +5% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reflect it; apply slight downward bias in next 3-5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out sharp changes in last 5-7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative swings, model tends to lag; add 1-2 days of lagged sentiment adjustment to forecast.
